findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Name the concrete seam the harness will monkeypatch to force exhaustion (e.g. override `verify_step_floor`/`step_floor` itself, not just `cfg.max_iterations`), since completion.py:237-238 raises a low `max_iterations` back up to `step_floor_min` and would prevent the intended insufficiency-only failure.
evidence: completion.py:237-238: `if cfg.max_iterations == DEFAULT_MAX_ITERATIONS or cfg.max_iterations < step_floor: cfg = replace(cfg, max_iterations=step_floor)`
verify_step_floor (completion.py:76-90) clamps to `step_floor_min` (default 160) as the minimum
Plan says 'harness override' but names no seam that bypasses this floor
findings.finding: The forced-exhaustion mechanism (steps 3 and 5) assumes a harness can impose a REDUCED step budget so attempt 1 fails insufficiency-only, but the verifier forces max_iterations UP to a computed floor (step_floor_min=160) whenever the configured value is below it, so a plain config override will be silently raised and attempt 1 will not exhaust as designed.
findings.location: Protocol steps 3 and 5 ('a deliberately REDUCED step budget (harness override)')
scenarios: Harness sets a low max_iterations expecting insufficiency; the floor raises it back and attempt 1 PASSes or exhausts elsewhere, invalidating the partial-bank precondition the whole experiment depends on
findings.suggested_fix: Monkeypatch `verify_step_floor` (or the `completion_verify_step_floor_min` config it reads) to a small value in the harness, rather than lowering `cfg.max_iterations`, so the reduced budget survives the floor clamp.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the verifier-facing decision rule co-located with the injected exclusion summary (advisory vs. hard-exclusion), matching the parent ticket's 'advisory not hard-exclusion to avoid permanent blind spots' constraint, so the treatment arm measures the frontier information rather than an untracked framing variable.
evidence: Plan step 5B: 'an exclusion summary injected into the verifier prompt'
Plan Why: exclusion list phrased '("already searched, found nothing: ...")'
Parent ticket 19ea-29af-ebb3-410b description: 'negative frontier, advisory not hard-exclusion to avoid permanent blind spots'

ABSENCE: no co-located processing/decision rule in the plan telling the verifier to treat the frontier as advisory rather than a do-not-re-search directive (T8 checklist item (b) and pink-elephant/instruction-locality item (e))
findings.finding: The exclusion summary injected into the verifier prompt (step 5B) defines its CONTENT and SIZE but not the DECISION RULE the verifier should apply to it; the parent ticket explicitly requires the frontier be 'advisory not hard-exclusion to avoid permanent blind spots,' yet the plan phrases the injected text only as a hard-sounding 'already searched, found nothing: ...' with no co-located instruction on how the verifier must weigh it.
findings.location: Protocol step 5(B) / step 4 (exclusion summary); Why paragraph ('already searched, found nothing: ...')
scenarios: Treatment arm verifier reads 'already searched X, found nothing' and stops re-examining X even though the reduced budget meant X was only partially searched — creating a permanent blind spot that biases the overlap-rate metric and could suppress a legitimate PASS
The measured 'measurably beats plain cache-seeded resume' verdict is confounded because the injected framing (hard vs advisory) is the untested variable, not the frontier information itself
findings.suggested_fix: In step 5B/step 4, pin the injected prompt framing as ADVISORY, e.g. prefix the summary with an explicit instruction such as 'The prior attempt searched the following without finding sufficient evidence; treat this as a hint to search ELSEWHERE FIRST, not a prohibition — re-search any location if you judge it necessary.' Document this framing so the metrics table attributes any overlap reduction to the frontier content, not to a hard-exclusion directive.

evidence: 1 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).

AC item 'Harness exists in the experiment worktree (throwaway; NOT pushed to Gerrit; no s' cites operational evidence (merge_gate) that lives outside the codebase but is not tagged [operator-attested]; prefix the checkbox text with [operator-attested] so the completion verifier accepts a recorded attestation instead of failing to find code proof.
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the decision rule for 'measurably beat' (e.g. B's overlap-rate lower on ALL tickets by >=X%, or a stated directional-consistency bar) so the go/no-go verdict is pre-registered rather than post-hoc.
evidence: 'Verdict comment: does the exclusion list measurably beat plain cache-seeded resume?'
Corpus is '>=2 real CLOSED tickets'; resume loop is '<=3 resume attempts' — too small for significance
subjective term 'measurably' with no stated decision rule
findings.finding: The verdict acceptance criterion asks whether the exclusion list 'measurably beat[s]' plain cache-seeded resume, but with only >=2 tickets and <=3 attempts per arm no statistical significance is possible and no interpretation of 'measurably' is stated (directional improvement? a minimum magnitude on which metric?).
findings.location: Acceptance criteria: 'does the exclusion list measurably beat plain cache-seeded resume?'
scenarios: Arm B shows lower overlap on one ticket but higher on the other — is that a 'beat'?
findings.suggested_fix: Add: 'measurably beat = treatment shows lower re-search overlap and fewer attempts-to-clean-close on EVERY ticket, reported as raw per-ticket deltas (no significance claim given n<=2); ties or mixed results => no-go.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Define the overlap-match predicate (e.g. compare resolved absolute paths for reads; exact-string match on grep pattern + target dir) so overlap rate is deterministically computable.
evidence: 'tool calls repeating any earlier attempt's arguments, same arm'
'derive per-criterion searched-set (paths read, patterns tried)'
no equality/normalization rule stated for path or pattern comparison
findings.finding: The core metric 're-search overlap rate' is defined as 'tool calls repeating any earlier attempt's arguments' but the matching predicate is unspecified — exact argument-string match vs normalized (resolved paths, canonicalized grep patterns). Different normalization yields materially different overlap numbers.
scenarios: Same file read via relative vs absolute path counted as non-overlap; equivalent grep patterns with reordered alternation counted as distinct

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the recovery action if attempt 1 fails other than insufficiency-only (e.g. re-tune the budget upward until the failure is insufficiency-only, and record the chosen budget per ticket).
evidence: 'run attempt 1 with a deliberately REDUCED step budget ... so it FAILs insufficiency-only'
no instruction for the case where the failure is not insufficiency-only
findings.finding: Step 3 requires attempt 1 to 'FAIL insufficiency-only' via a reduced budget, but the plan gives no fallback if the reduced budget instead produces a genuine criterion FAIL (adverse judgment) rather than insufficiency, which would invalidate the resume premise.
scenarios: Reduced budget yields a hard FAIL verdict on some criterion; executor unsure whether to re-tune the budget or proceed

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State how run-to-run LLM variance is controlled (e.g. multiple repetitions per arm with a fixed/reported temperature or seed, and report spread not just point deltas) so a 'measurably beats' verdict is defensible rather than a single-sample artifact.
evidence: Plan runs one CONTROL and one TREATMENT pass per ticket with no stated repetition or fixed seed
Metrics are per-attempt deltas (overlap rate, PASS-per-step, attempts, cost) between two single arms
LLM tool-call selection is non-deterministic; overlap and steps vary run-to-run independent of the treatment
findings.finding: The experiment's central claim ('does the exclusion list MEASURABLY reduce re-search overlap and steps-to-verdict') is measured with a single run per (ticket, arm) across only >=2 tickets, against a non-deterministic LLM verifier and with no repetition/seeding, so arm A-vs-B deltas will be confounded by run-to-run variance and cannot support a 'measurable' verdict.
findings.location: Protocol step 6 (Metrics table) and Acceptance criteria (verdict comment: 'does the exclusion list measurably beat plain cache-seeded resume?')
scenarios: Treatment appears to 'win' or 'lose' on one ticket purely from sampling noise; the go/no-go recommendation rests on an unreproducible single-sample delta

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Note that the per-arm temp cache dirs are removed on harness teardown (e.g. tempfile.TemporaryDirectory) so no orphaned cache copies accumulate.
evidence: 'monkeypatches cache_dir ... to return a per-arm temp dir'
'its populated cache is then COPIED once and each resume arm reads its own identical copy'
no teardown/removal of temp dirs mentioned
findings.finding: The harness creates per-arm isolated cache namespaces in temp dirs (create + consume defined) but no RETIRE/cleanup step is stated for the copied caches and temp dirs after the experiment.
scenarios: Repeated PoC runs accumulate orphaned per-arm cache temp dirs

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State whether the harness extends/copies docs/experiments/diag_runaway_transcript.py (tool-factory wrapping + _VERIFY_MIN_STEPS override) rather than re-implementing transcript capture and forced exhaustion from scratch.
evidence: Plan step 2: 'wrap the verifier's tool executor in-harness (monkeypatch at the workflow seam) to log every tool call with full arguments (file paths read, grep patterns, dirs listed) per criterion.'
Plan step 3: 'run attempt 1 with a deliberately REDUCED step budget (harness override) so it FAILs insufficiency-only'.

docs/experiments/diag_runaway_transcript.py:84-90 wraps pai_tools factories 'filesystem_tools' / 'grounding_tools' / 'rebar_tools' and logs {tool, args, kwargs, result_preview, is_error, is_empty_sentinel} to a local JSONL.
docs/experiments/diag_runaway_transcript.py:105-107 sets _completion._VERIFY_MIN_STEPS = floor to force cheap bounded exhaustion — the same 'reduced step budget' knob the plan needs.
docs/experiments/diag-runaway-transcript.md:20 names this 'the sanctioned lower-the-iteration-limit pattern'.
Both are throwaway experiment harnesses, so reuse (not production extraction) is the intended efficiency.
findings.finding: The transcript-capture and forced-exhaustion mechanism (steps 2-3) reinvents the existing experiment harness docs/experiments/diag_runaway_transcript.py, which already wraps the same verifier tool factories to log full-argument tool calls and lowers _VERIFY_MIN_STEPS to force cheap exhaustion.
scenarios: Author builds a fresh tool-wrapping logger and step-floor override from scratch, duplicating diag_runaway_transcript.py and risking a different (weaker) argument-capture shape than the proven one.
The per-criterion argument grouping the plan needs is easier to add on top of the existing content-free JSONL logger than to re-derive.
findings.suggested_fix: In steps 2-3, cite docs/experiments/diag_runaway_transcript.py as the base: reuse its _wrap/_patch_factory tool-logging (which already captures full args and preserves pydantic-ai signatures) and its _VERIFY_MIN_STEPS floor override, and note the only additions this PoC needs — per-criterion grouping of the transcript and per-arm cache_dir monkeypatch.
